clue.text: Criticise Oscar's play after dismissing initial view

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: dismissing the initial means the first letter of the word for play is dropped

parts.note: a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A critic tears into Oscar Wilde's play, having first sent away the person who began it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like Wilde or the award; it is just the phonetic-alphabet letter, with 's meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, sweeping view of a landscape or scene.

clue.text: A lot of enthusiasm after receiving tense letter from Athens

indicators.note: receiving means the shortened word takes the next letter inside it
a lot of, but not all, means the last letter of the word for enthusiasm is cut

parts.note: zeal is eager enthusiasm
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone waits eagerly for a nervous letter arriving from Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims ZEAL to ZEA; 'receiving' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeta is the sixth character of the Greek alphabet, so a letter as written in Athens.

clue.text: Leaders of harsh extremists in central region hang together

indicators.note: in means those two letters sit inside the word for central region

parts.note: the core is the central region of something

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, so the first letter of each of the next two words is taken

explanation.surface: Radical leaders in the heartland of a country stick together.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that cohere stick together or form a unified, consistent whole.

clue.text: Support limiting jump in business discussions

indicators.note: limiting means bounding on both sides, so the word for support goes round the next piece

parts.note: a stalk is the stem supporting a leaf or flower
a hop is a small jump

explanation.surface: Backing that caps a leap in the company's talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop talk is conversation about one's work or trade, the business chat of colleagues.

clue.text: Driver wildly interrupting acclamation

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the word for acclamation

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of acclamation
to run a riot is to behave wildly, so 'a riot' stands for wildly

explanation.surface: A motorist goes berserk, cutting into the applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' is not an anagram signal here: it is a synonym for A RIOT, as in running riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer drives a chariot, so is a driver in the ancient sense.

clue.text: Edge of wheel following path round front of garden

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: round means the word for path wraps around the next letter

parts.note: a lane is a narrow path or road

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A wheel rim rolls along a path past the garden's front.
explanation.definitionFit: A flange is the projecting rim on a railway wheel that keeps it on the track.

clue.text: Get away and really appreciate mountain scenery?

definitions.meaning: to flee somewhere remote, escaping pursuit
taking to something means liking it, so whimsically liking high ground

explanation.surface: A holiday-maker escapes and enjoys the mountain views.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to run off and hide; read literally, it is warming to the hills.

clue.text: Setter in variety of ascot ties is a smart figure

indicators.note: in means the setter's name sits inside the rearranged letters
a variety of the letters means they are rearranged

parts.note: Phi is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker among an assortment of fancy neckwear cuts a dapper figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges ASCOT TIES; 'in' puts PHI, the setter, among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophisticate is a worldly, refined person, a smart figure in society.

clue.text: Paying after trees get bit of trim in seasonal visit

indicators.note: after places the paying piece behind the earlier ones

parts.note: firs are conifer trees

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter

parts.note: footing the bill means paying it

explanation.surface: Settling a bill once the trees are tidied, on a festive call.
explanation.walkthrough: First-footing is a Scottish New Year custom: being the first visitor across the threshold after midnight.
explanation.definitionFit: The custom is a particular visit made at Hogmanay, so a seasonal one.

clue.text: I criticise including circle in maroon

indicators.note: including means the word for criticise holds the next letter

parts.note: to slate someone is to criticise them severely
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a dark red colour, circle and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maroon' looks like the colour; here it is the verb, to strand.
explanation.definitionFit: To maroon someone is to leave them stranded and cut off, alone.

clue.text: Vegetable: two, not one, a bargain

indicators.note: not one means the letter standing for one is removed

parts.note: a pair is two
a snip is a bargain, a cheap buy

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's offer: two for the price of one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' removes I (one) from PAIR, giving PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The parsnip is a pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Religious figure boarding rocket beginning to animate TV show?

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the religious figure goes inside the word for rocket

parts.note: to rocket is to soar upwards
the Pope heads the Catholic Church

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pontiff climbs aboard a spacecraft, just the start of an animated programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama, an example of a TV programme.

clue.text: Everyone's aware of it, so pretence collapses

indicators.note: something that collapses falls apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: When everyone knows the truth, the act falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: An open secret is something supposedly confidential that is in fact widely known.

clue.text: Pointed shapes visible in strobe lighting

indicators.note: visible in means the letters can be seen inside these words

explanation.surface: Spiky shapes flash into view under strobe lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger-shaped marks used in printing, plural of obelus.

clue.text: Tart pulled over French street walker

parts.note: a flan is an open tart

indicators.note: pulled over means turned back, so the French word is written backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A police stop: a prostitute pulled over on a French street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'street walker' reads as one phrase; 'street' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A flâneur is a man who strolls idly about town observing life, an urban walker.

clue.text: Hold back support over Middle Eastern country shifting leader

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the second in this down entry

parts.note: a rest is something that supports, like an armrest

indicators.note: shifting the leader means the first letter is moved elsewhere in the word

parts.note: Iran is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Restrain support for a Middle Eastern state undergoing a change of ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting leader' moves the I of IRAN to make RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to keep in check or prevent from acting.

clue.text: Turn away, eager to miss new sullen look

indicators.note: to miss means a letter is left out

parts.note: keen means eager
a pout is a sulky pushing-out of the lips

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a keen suitor, who leaves sulking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to miss new' drops N from KEEN, giving KEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep out is to bar entry, turning visitors away.

clue.text: Old US President amongst quintet in shot

indicators.note: amongst means the president's initials sit inside the number

parts.note: a quintet is five
FDR is Franklin Delano Roosevelt

explanation.surface: An elderly American leader among five people in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: An off drive is a cricket stroke hit straight back on the off side; 'shot' looks like a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a drive is an attacking stroke, and this one goes to the off side.

clue.text: Polar hero, one in old group that's recalled

indicators.note: in means the letter for one sits inside
recalled means called back, so the word for group is turned round

parts.note: a set is a group
A is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An explorer from an old team is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Lawrence Oates walked out to his death on Scott's Antarctic expedition of 1912.
explanation.definitionFit: Oates died heroically on Scott's doomed South Pole expedition.

clue.text: Members of house party brought in numberless performers

indicators.note: brought in means the party goes inside the shortened word
numberless means without the letter for number

parts.note: turns are music-hall performers
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Members of a party house invited to an event full of anonymous acts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numberless' drops N (number) from TURNS; 'house' is a royal dynasty, not a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the royal house of England from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Poor sci-fi, in translation, unlikely to make you excited

indicators.note: translation turns the words into something else, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Badly translated science fiction is a real bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Soporific means sleep-inducing, the opposite of exciting.

clue.text: Place to gradually advance commitment

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for Place in addresses
to edge forward is to advance gradually

explanation.surface: A spot from which to creep forward on a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise, a commitment to do something.

clue.text: Lively daughter returned, following in fast vehicle

indicators.note: following places the reversed piece after the next word
returned means sent back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: racy means lively and spirited

explanation.surface: A spirited daughter comes home and then speeds off in a racing car.
explanation.definitionFit: IndyCar is the American open-wheel racing series, and its cars are very fast.

clue.text: Runs into bar in trailer?

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar in the sense of except, as in 'all bar one'
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a pub with a caravan in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A film trailer is a short extract from the movie, shown as a preview.

clue.text: Staff boasted

definitions.meaning: the team of people working on a ship or project
an old past tense of crow, to brag

explanation.surface: Employees bragged.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a working team and, archaically, crowed or bragged.

clue.text: Time off in bed (inter alia)?

parts.note: a break from work spent, among other things, tending flowerbeds; bed suggests lying in

explanation.surface: A worker on leave spends much of it lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Gardening leave is a British term: an employee who is leaving is paid to stay away from work during their notice period, free to potter in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names paid absence from the office, punningly spent in the flowerbeds.
